data.one_liner: A customizable tooltip and popup overlay widget with optional target highlighting.
data.what_it_does: Wraps any Flutter widget to display an informational popup or tooltip when triggered. It supports arrow direction adjustments, custom widget content, and a highlight feature to draw attention to the target element. Popups can be controlled programmatically or dismissed via gesture triggers.
use_when: You want to display contextual tooltips or info dialogs pointing directly to a specific UI widget.
You need feature walkthroughs or onboarding highlights that focus the user's attention on a widget.
Standard Flutter tooltips are too basic and you require rich custom content like inputs or styled text.
avoid_when: You only need simple, native system-style hover tooltips (use Flutter's built-in Tooltip).
You need standard modal screen navigation or full-screen dialogs.
strengths: Provides built-in target highlighting to spotlight wrapped widgets.
Supports custom widget builders via `customContent` alongside default text styling.
Handles automatic arrow direction and constraints calculation.
weaknesses: README examples contain slightly outdated syntax (shows `customContent: Container(...)` while v4.0.0 changelog notes it now requires a builder `() => Widget`).
Complex nested overlay positioning can occasionally encounter edge cases as noted in constraint fix changelogs.
data.minimal_example:
InfoPopupWidget(
  contentTitle: 'Info Popup Details',
  child: Icon(
    Icons.info,
    color: Colors.pink,
  ),
)
